posts.text: Fwd from @ 📝 Here we go again 📝 French protests losing momentum The sixth Saturday of protests in France takes place under tight security, though turnout continues to decline steadily . On November 21, authorities deployed 70,000 police and gendarmes across the country, while Paris expects only 15 to 30 thousand demonstrators. According to the Interior Ministry, across the country — excluding Paris — authorities recorded 44 actions that drew only 2,200 people. A week earlier at the same time, 9,800 demonstrators took to the streets in the regions. At the moment, Paris remains relatively calm, with Lyon becoming the main flashpoint, where the prefecture banned demonstrations in the city center and mobilized a thousand security forces. Despite the ban, three unsanctioned columns started there. Shortly after, CRS special forces deployed tear gas to stop the march at the Garibaldi metro station, while demonstrators managed to erect a barricade on Thermes Street. Overall, the Interior Ministry describes the situation across the country as calm: only seven people have been detained so far compared to 24 a week ago. 📌 Turnout has noticeably declined, the Saturday protest format is clearly running out of steam. Nevertheless, authorities are not easing up, as the protest remains politically unresolved. Trade unions have already scheduled a new strike for December 1, while presidential elections in April 2027 loom increasingly large on the agenda. The protesters clearly are not waiting for concessions from the current government — they are formulating demands to present to the next cabinet. Only a change in power is unlikely to change anything. #protests #France 👁 @evropar — on the brink of Europe's death 💸 Support us Original msg
